Much like the party that Costa throws for Tommy, Project X seems determined to be the big, explosive, definitive conclusion to the “one crazy party” sub-genre of comedy. It has everything that could possibly excite a heterosexual teenage boy in the early 2010s – alcohol, drugs, boobs, stunts, implied sex, and everything in between. And for the most part, its mission is successful; later movies that delve into this sandbox, like Office Christmas Party , don’t quite have their hearts in the same place, and it comes off feeling more tired than energetic. My feelings on Project X are actually pretty similar to Office Christmas Party – the debauchery is hardly engaging, and since that’s what the whole film is supposedly barreling towards, it has to be pretty compelling to break through. At least Project X has the excuse of solely focusing on the party. I am not exaggerating when I say there is nothing more to this film than the insanity and excess that comes from an out-of-control hormonal rager. Most of the characters are irredeemably annoying, but that’s nothing new for a film of this caliber. Their values (which, as far as I can tell, bear little difference from the movie as a whole) feel antiquated, even for 2012. It may have intentionally provided an apex (which, in turn, may have killed the sub-genre), but that doesn’t quite dovetail with the quality of the movie itself, as hard as it tries to make itself stand out. It doesn’t matter how cool you were or weren’t in high school; the shenanigans in Project X are more exhausting than anything else.

Project X si rivela una discreta commedia adolescenziale costruita con l'efficace espediente del falso documentario. Al di là della componente comica, il film propone una critica agli eccessi della gioventù e al bisogno quasi ossessivo di ottenere accettazione e popolarità. La gigantesca festa, dominata da alcol, droga e sesso, diventa così il simbolo di una ribellione adolescenziale destinata a sfuggire completamente di mano. La scelta di alternare riprese con telecamera a mano, cellulari e dashcam rende il racconto dinamico e immersivo, trasmettendo allo spettatore il progressivo deterioramento della situazione e la perdita di controllo dei protagonisti. È proprio attraverso questo caos crescente che il film racconta le conseguenze della ricerca esasperata di approvazione sociale. Il finale, volutamente sopra le righe, risulta forse fin troppo esagerato e poco credibile, ma si inserisce perfettamente nel tono folle e irriverente dell'opera. Nel complesso, Project X è una commedia divertente e coinvolgente che, dietro la sua leggerezza, riesce anche a offrire qualche spunto di riflessione sugli eccessi e sulle fragilità dell'adolescenza.

This is a cultural artifact that offers nothing more than a time capsule into the worst aspects of 2012 culture. That’s sounds harsh but considering I was the exact age/grade of the characters in this movie in 2012, I think I have a modest level of authority to speak on this topic. I think it’s really entertaining for the most part despite how unbelievable it was. But I’m not going to say it’s a good movie that holds up to time. It was never meant to be that anyway.
